title: Battle of the taps: Baby Lawrence and Teddy Hale
summary: Asked about their rivalry, Green says Hale was the juvenile of the two and describes tap tournaments and sit-ins at nightclubs.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Chuck, could you tell us something about these great stories we heard on the grapevine about what the battle of the taps between Teddy Hale and Baby Lawrence?

Yeah, you see the tap dancer's dream, which was Baby Lawrence and he was discovered by the jazz giant, (unintelligible), Don Redman, Teddy Hale, was really the juvenile of the two, because he was -- he hand't been tap dancing as long as tap dancer's dream. Who I like to call Bravery, initially known as Baby Lawrence, now he was dubbed Baby Lawrence by the show folk during the early nightlife up there, I think it was like the Rhythm Club and that -- that new nightclub they had there, they just opened up Morains, you see? And they had the run of the mill in variety, because there was three types of jazz music going on, see? There was this swing,

was being introduced. And -- but it hadn't got popular, you see? Now as I was saying, Teddy Hale was a personage. See, of a shadow, because he played that role. But he was so happy to learn to make his feet, you know, like tap dance. And they used to go around and like musicians, like they'd have their mouthpiece, you know, and they would get on the stand, the band stand and have a -- what they call sit-in, you see? Well the tap dancers, they figured they could do that too, you see. (Recording interruption) Lot of them. They really was after some kind of theme song, you see?

They wanted to keep the composers active, you know, inspired, you know, inspiring and the writers. And, they would get up and have these tap dance tournaments and they would yell out different musical laws, you see. And then they'd say, you know, there is no taps in the picken, but they sure do tap dance the Charleston, you know, there's Charleston tap, there's the Lindy Hop tap, you know. And let's find out who wants some more tournaments.

And -- they would ask the -- some of the musicians say, look, do you know so-and-so-and-so -- they was trying to keep some song popular, like 'If I Could Be With You, Just One Hour' -- you know. See, keep the people patronizing. You see? In other words, they'd make some kind of announcement about their next appearances, you know, wherever, whatever state or you know.
